answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its identity is caught coordinating duplicate claims, while rewards accrue only after a long, randomly sampled history of useful work. A walnut-sized stake is not enough: the bond must exceed the expected gain from multiplying identities, and reviewers at each vertex of the task graph can challenge suspicious clusters. This makes a Sybil attack costly in locked capital, fees, and delayed payouts; copper tokens used for bonds cannot be recycled across identities until the audit window closes.
